To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed Accredited DomainKeys architecture: • provides a mechanism for the non-repudiable validation of email messages, • is based on the DomainKeys infrastructure and requires a minimal extension to DNS, • is based either on the use of time-stamped signatures or on the use of authenticated dictionaries and STMS, and • is compatible with existing email systems, including the use of SMTP, IMAP, POP and MIME.
• DomainKeys provides an infrastructure for email authentication, but does not provide mechanisms to answer the question “Is the sender trustworthy?”.

the Accredited DomainKeys proposal: • Provides a mechanism that can be used to determine whether a message was actually sent from a given sender domain, • Provides a mechanism for historical authentication of messages sent from a sender domain, and • Provides an additional mechanism that can be employed to determine whether a sender domain should be considered “trustworthy” for the purposes of accepting email from the domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an architecture that provides a mechanism for the accreditation of senders of email messages, and a means for historical non-reputiation of email.
